_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-17 · Sky165 — the grid is built and live. The spreadsheet version of it is next.
_status: The grid you asked for is built: credential names down the side, every college across the top, credit-recommendation units in the cells — green for what a college already has, brown (in brackets) for what it could still get. It shows 434 credentials across 118 colleges, and about a sixth of the grid is filled in, with 59% of those credentials showing at least one college that could pick them up. Your four calls are all in it. Building it turned up one real problem: Cañada College was appearing twice, because two parts of our own pipeline spell its name differently — one of those columns had all of Cañada's opportunities and the other was empty, which looks exactly like a college with nothing available. That is fixed. Next is letting the grid leave as a spreadsheet, which is how it actually reaches a college.

items.text: You said 115 credit colleges and 4 noncredit campuses. The 115 matches exactly. We can only find 3 noncredit — North Orange Continuing Education, San Diego College of Continuing Education, and Calbright. The fourth is Mt. SAC's noncredit side, and it does not exist as its own entry anywhere in MAP, so it cannot be a column until it does. Worth deciding whether MAP should carry it separately.

Four credentials appear on the tab as "unclassified" even though the Credential Reference already knows them by name. They are not broken, just not linked up, so they sink to the bottom of the list where nobody finds them. Fixing it is a naming decision rather than code — we can walk you through the four whenever you want. Separately, two statewide exhibits match no college at all — nobody has adopted them, nobody is even a candidate, and they carry no credit recommendations. They look like empty records rather than real opportunities; worth a glance at the same time.

Sweep the automated tests for checks that measure distance in characters rather than testing the actual thing. One of them had been failing for a day, and not because anything was broken: a previous session added an explanatory comment, which pushed the text it was looking for out of range. It went red on the commit that documented itself best. There are likely others.

Decide how far the Finance phrase should reach. You said it should not open the whole workplan, and you are right — today it opens Contracts plus about 30 other tables, because the check accepts any phrase at all. But the obvious fix goes too far: locking Finance to 'only Finance' would also shut it out of Budget and Implementation Funding, which Finance genuinely needs. The right answer is that a tab used by two groups accepts either phrase, and only the CPL-only tabs stop accepting the Finance one. Say go and we will write the plan first — this changes who can read what, live, and getting it wrong locks people out in the middle of their work.

Turn the list of sites (CPL, C&I, CIP, GR, Finance) into a proper table instead of code. Right now three separate lists describe the sites and none of them is in charge — they already disagree, since CIP is a site with no phrase. This is what would let 'what is in Finance' be one list instead of two, and what an Admin filter per site would read.

Three questions for Jenni, in one go. (1) Confirm the Basic Skills code pairing — this single answer unblocks the first three build phases of the noncredit CIP work. (2) Two codes are in real use but missing from her list: 32.0199 (60 programs) and 35.0101 (16). (3) The big one: can a non-CDCP category be CTE at all? That decides roughly 1,300 programs, and CTE is funding-bearing.

Decide where a confirmed noncredit category gets saved. Right now the plan was the browser's own storage, which is wrong for something that affects funding — it vanishes on another machine and nobody can see who decided what. Recommend a proper table that records who confirmed it and when.

Six new decision rights are on the register with nobody's name against them. Start with DR-13, the workplan itself — it is the most public thing the project publishes, four of its tables can be edited in the page by anyone holding the team phrase, and a wrong figure reaches the live dashboard on the next morning's run.

The project's always-loaded instructions file is still twice the size it should be. This session archived one old session write-up and rewrote a section instead of adding to it, but that is holding the line, not fixing it. The finished workstreams — the EACR filters, the team phrases, the sign-in work — are history now and belong in the reference folder. Every line costs every future session.

Let the new grid leave as a spreadsheet. That is the whole point of the brown numbers being what other colleges actually earned rather than the most the exhibit allows — a spreadsheet gets emailed to a college and read months later, with nobody around to explain it. The export has to say exactly what the screen says, over the same 118 colleges.

Have a look at the grid on the live site and tell us whether it reads. It is 434 rows by 118 columns, so it scrolls sideways — that is unavoidable at this width, but whether the density is useful is your call. The mock looked right to you; this is the first time it exists with all the real data in it.

Fix the Cañada spelling where it starts, not just where it shows. One part of the dashboard generator writes the name with mangled accented characters and another writes it correctly, so the same college arrived under two names. We have folded them together, but the generator should stop producing two spellings — and nobody has checked whether other accented names are affected.

A question about the grid worth your eye. About 350 times, a college has already taken a credential but claimed fewer units than most colleges claim for the same one — 172 credentials, roughly 1,100 units between them and their peers. These are probably the easiest wins on the whole tab, because the college, the faculty contact and the review already exist; the ask is to extend an agreement, not start one. We have NOT put it on the grid, because it means a second number inside the green squares and that changes how the whole thing looks. Do you want to see a version with it?
